_comment: Central launch config for all agents. Consumed by launcher.sh, watchdog.sh, and supervisor. Change settings here, not in shell scripts.

chat._maxSessionTurns_comment: Cold-start backstop only — chat is interactive and never rotates mid-conversation. Consulted at boot to avoid resuming a session that already grew past 250 turns (e.g. after a kill). High because chat conversation continuity is valuable. Active ops turn-count rotation: see ops.maxSessionTurns.
chat._effort_comment: 2026-10-04 — latency. Chat turns were dominated by thinking time, not tools: in the latency benchmark a memory question spent 8s in four tool calls and ~18s thinking before replying, and one watchlist ask thought for ~4.5 min before its first tool call (blocking the next message). Low still thinks adaptively when a question needs it. Revert by deleting this line + restarting the chat supervisor process.
chat._disallowedTools_comment: Servers removed from the chat agent's context entirely (allowedTools does NOT do that under bypassPermissions). The installation lists its own per agent in agent/local/config/agents.json `disallowed_tools` (appended to this array by the supervisor): the connectors with zero calls on that agent over a month or two, each re-read on every turn otherwise. To give an agent one back, delete its line there and restart that supervisor process.

ops._disallowedTools_comment: Servers removed from this tier's prefix: the installation's own list in agent/local/config/agents.json `disallowed_tools` (appended to this array by the supervisor), the servers with ZERO calls on this tier in 30 days (cost-efficiency-derived.json mcp_tool_listing, per-tier calls_30d). Per-agent deny, not an account change: the user's own sessions and the other tiers keep them. To give a tier one back, delete its line there and restart that supervisor.
ops._model_comment: Flipped opus→claude-sonnet-5 on 2026-07-02 (the user's call: everything to Sonnet except one financial-analysis job). Sonnet 5 is near-Opus quality at ~1/3 the price — moves email triage, deep synthesis, chrome jobs, and Gmail catchup off Opus. The ONE remaining Opus job of that kind is the installation's weekly financial monitor, which runs as a dedicated ephemeral `claude -p --model $EDVA_MODEL_OPUS (claude-opus-5-5 since 2026-10-06, pinned in agent/config/models.env)` (bumped from claude-opus-4-8 on 2026-07-24; see its trigger script) rather than through this supervisor. Reversible in one line: set model back to opus + restart. 2026-10-06: claude-sonnet-5 → claude-sonnet-5-5 (the user asked for the 5.5 models; same $2/$10 price; verified on Max — a launchd job ran claude-sonnet-5-5 that day). Must equal EDVA_MODEL_SONNET in models.env.
ops._effort_comment: Defensive explicit setting — Opus 4.7 on Max defaults to xhigh per Anthropic 2026-04-16 announcement, but making it explicit at spawn time guarantees the level regardless of any future default shift. Session-scoped: changes require supervisor restart.
ops._maxSessionTurns_comment: Rotate to a fresh Claude session after this many DISPATCHES (the key kept its historical name). Until 2026-10-04 the supervisor compared it against num_turns summed across dispatches — tool steps, not dispatches — so one 20-step job used up most of the cap and the tiers rotated every ~4.5 dispatches (465 of 704 rotations in the 14d to 2026-10-04 were 'turn-count cap 20'), each paying a cold floor write plus MCP respawn. The context guard (index.mjs startContextGuard, context-guard.mjs) is the primary bound on context size; this cap is only a coarse backstop on session age. Fires at a turn boundary even while the queue is busy. Set 0 to disable. Change requires supervisor restart.
ops._gmailTriageTarget_comment: Per-message Gmail triage dispatches (source gmail:<messageId>) are POSTed to this tier's webhook instead of the ops session (2026-10-04, agent/supervisor/triage-route.mjs). ops-light runs the same model and the same CLAUDE.md at --effort medium with no Chrome; a triage turn needs neither xhigh nor Chrome now that the dispatch carries the body/headers/Jev verdict/history and the agent reads `triage-rules core` + one section. Mail addressed to Edva (command channel) and batch/catch-up/storm dispatches stay on ops. Falls back to ops whenever ops-light is unhealthy or the POST fails. ROLLBACK: set to "ops" (or null) and restart the ops supervisor.
ops._emailInboundMode_comment: How allowlisted mail to Edva's own address is handled (2026-10-04). "oneshot" (default when absent): the /email-inbound route spawns bin/email-inbound-run — a stateless claude -p with built-in tools off and one strict MCP server (read-only wiki/recall/travel/calendar + escalate_to_ops + mkt_apply); the reply is sent in code to the sender only, and anything needing an action is escalated into this session. "session": dispatch every allowlisted email straight into the ops session (the pre-2026-10-04 path) — the rollback. Read from config at startup: restart the ops supervisor after changing it. See jobs/email-inbound.md.
ops._excludeDynamicPromptSections_comment: Spawn claude with --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections (only when the installed CLI supports it) so today's date/cwd/env info move out of the system prompt and the cached floor stays byte-identical across days and rotations (2026-10-04). Defaults ON for every supervisor agent when absent; set false on an agent to opt it out.

ops-light._disallowedTools_comment: Servers removed from this tier's prefix: the installation's own list in agent/local/config/agents.json `disallowed_tools` (appended to this array by the supervisor), the servers with ZERO calls on this tier in 30 days (cost-efficiency-derived.json mcp_tool_listing, per-tier calls_30d). ops-light._comment: Sonnet sibling of ops. Added 2026-06-17 (Lever B of the June-15 cost re-architecture — see docs/cost-rearchitecture-june2026.md). Cron/webhook jobs whose job-routing.json model is NOT opus route here instead of ops; webhook-auth.sh picks the port pair by job tier. Runs its OWN lean cwd (ops-light-agent) with a Chrome-LESS .mcp.json so it doesn't double the Chrome footprint on a RAM-constrained host. NO gmailPubsubPort: the Gmail push/catchup path stays single-instance on ops (index.mjs gates gmail features on the presence of gmailPubsubPort). State + event logs isolate under state/ops-light + logs/supervisor-ops-light; queue persists to dispatcher-queue-ops-light.json. Deep-synthesis jobs (daily/weekly/monthly-summary, nightly-review, …) and Chrome jobs stay on ops via webhook-auth.sh overrides.
ops-light._compactOnContext_comment: Cron-only tier: the context guard rotates where it would otherwise /compact (2026-10-04). Jobs here keep state in playbooks/state files, not conversation history, so a /compact summary is never read back. See context-guard.mjs. ops leaves this unset (compacts).

ops-haiku._disallowedTools_comment: Servers removed from this tier's prefix: the installation's own list in agent/local/config/agents.json `disallowed_tools` (appended to this array by the supervisor), the servers with ZERO calls on this tier in 30 days (cost-efficiency-derived.json mcp_tool_listing, per-tier calls_30d). Per-agent deny, not an account change: the user's own sessions and the other tiers keep them. To give a tier one back, delete its line there and restart that supervisor.
ops-haiku._comment: Haiku sibling of ops/ops-light. Added 2026-06-17 (Lever B Haiku tier — see docs/cost-rearchitecture-june2026.md). Cron/webhook jobs whose job-routing.json model is 'haiku' (the pure scan/watch jobs: watchers, location-ambient, p1-resolution-scan, etc.) route here instead of ops-light; webhook-auth.sh picks the port pair by job tier (haiku→9072, sonnet→9082, opus→9092) with a haiku→light→heavy health fallback. Measured Sonnet→Haiku saving on these jobs: about two thirds. Same lean Chrome-LESS cwd pattern as ops-light; NO gmailPubsubPort (gmail stays single-instance on ops). State+logs isolate under state/ops-haiku + logs/supervisor-ops-haiku; queue persists to dispatcher-queue-ops-haiku.json.
ops-haiku._maxSessionTurns_comment: 30 dispatches (was 20 tool turns ≈ 4.5 dispatches before 2026-10-04). Same rationale as ops.maxSessionTurns.
ops-haiku._compactOnContext_comment: Cron-only tier: rotate instead of /compact. Same rationale as ops-light.compactOnContext.
